description: The same first-send approval with the channel written lowercase ("gmail") collapses to the same delivery key as the uppercase-channel first send.
why_it_exists: The delivery-key basis trims and uppercases the channel before hashing, but until this case nothing pinned that fold on its own: every other delivery-key scenario writes the channel already uppercased ("GMAIL"), and wf4-delivery-key-recipient-normalisation varies the recipient and the channel together, so its assertion stays green on the recipient fold alone. A regression that dropped only the channel uppercasing would therefore have passed the whole suite, and a retry of an approved send whose action row carried "gmail" instead of "GMAIL" would have hashed to a second send_key and a second communication_id -- the same duplicate-send failure mode that F-02 widened the key to close. This case holds the recipient and every other basis field byte-identical to wf4-delivery-key-first-send so the channel fold is the only thing under test.
assertions: send_key is identical to the uppercase-channel first-send key
the channel is uppercased before entering the basis, so "gmail" and "GMAIL" hash alike
no other basis field differs from wf4-delivery-key-first-send
